macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Markets rebound as oil retreats, but geopolitical and inflation worries persist
items.summary: U.S. stock futures edged higher as markets steadied after renewed U.S.-Iran tensions and a surge in oil prices. Reuters said investors remained focused on whether higher energy costs could revive inflation pressures and unsettle bonds and equities.

items.title: Stagflation fears return as oil surges and central banks stay cautious
items.summary: Reuters reported that renewed conflict in the Gulf has revived stagflation concerns, with oil prices back near $100 and government borrowing costs rising on inflation angst. The report also noted the European Central Bank left rates unchanged but signaled that further tightening may still be possible.

items.title: Asian and European markets mixed as oil-driven inflation fears weigh on sentiment
items.summary: Reuters noted that Asian shares advanced while gains were capped by higher oil prices, and European shares rose in choppy trading led by a rebound in technology stocks. MarketScreener also highlighted Australian shares wobbling as Fed caution tempered optimism tied to lower oil prices.

items.title: Fed caution and global rate expectations keep bond markets under pressure
items.summary: Reuters said the U.S. dollar held firm and Japanese government bond yields hit a 30-year high as investors priced in the inflation impact of rising oil prices. Reuters also reported that ECB policymakers are expected by some investors to deliver additional quarter-point rate hikes by year-end.

items.title: PepsiCo beats revenue expectations despite softer North American demand
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that PepsiCo’s second-quarter net revenue rose 6.4% to $24.2 billion, topping expectations even as the company said U.S. consumers were tightening budgets. CNBC also flagged PepsiCo among the biggest premarket stock movers after the mixed earnings report.

items.title: AstraZeneca falls after disappointing heart treatment trial
items.summary: FT reported AstraZeneca shares slid after a heart-treatment trial disappointed investors. The move was also highlighted in FT’s news feed as one of the day’s notable stock reactions.

items.title: SpaceX set to join the Nasdaq-100, triggering index-fund buying
items.summary: CNN reported that SpaceX is set to officially join the Nasdaq-100, which should prompt automatic purchases from index funds. Reuters-linked coverage also noted strong interest in large-cap tech and semiconductor names as part of broader index reshuffling effects.

items.title: U.S. imposes new tariffs on 60 trading partners, adding to trade tensions
items.summary: Reuters reported that the U.S. imposed new tariffs of 10% and 12.5% on goods from 60 trading partners, including the EU and China. The move increases the risk of higher consumer prices and further complicates the macroeconomic outlook.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox says Game Pass has not grown as expected
items.summary: Xbox leadership reportedly admitted that Game Pass has fallen tens of millions of subscribers short of Microsoft’s earlier growth targets, signaling a rethink of the service’s trajectory.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports are now available on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: Activision has released Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and Black Ops 2 on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5, though the launch is described as expensive for buyers.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced hits a major Steam player peak
items.summary: The Assassin’s Creed Black Flag revival has reportedly reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, the highest peak for any game in the franchise so far.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with a livestream event
items.summary: Niantic is hosting a special live celebration for Pokémon Go’s 10th anniversary, with announcements and surprises revealed during the event.

items.title: Nintendo will shut down Mario Kart Tour in September
items.summary: Nintendo has announced that Mario Kart Tour will end service in September after seven years, marking the retirement of one of its long-running mobile titles.

items.title: Sony plans to end physical PlayStation discs for new games in 2028
items.summary: Sony is reportedly moving new PlayStation releases to digital-only format after January 2028, a major industry shift that is already drawing backlash.

items.title: Fortnite adds an American Dad crossover bundle
items.summary: Epic Games has released a new American Dad bundle in Fortnite’s item shop, though fans have criticized the crossover for not including Roger.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 will get its own standalone launcher
items.summary: Black Ops 6 is set to separate from the unified Call of Duty HQ hub and operate through its own dedicated launcher.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit over Fortnite leaks
items.summary: Epic Games has reached a settlement in its case against a former contractor accused of leaking confidential details about upcoming Fortnite collaborations.

items.title: Obsidian reportedly begins work on a new Fallout game
items.summary: Jason Schreier reports that Obsidian Entertainment has started development on a brand-new Fallout project, renewing interest in the franchise’s future.

items.title: Ubisoft announces The Crew Motorfest for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Ubisoft says The Crew Motorfest will arrive on Switch 2 on October 8, with physical retail copies including a digital download code.

items.title: Bethesda and Xbox restructuring continues after layoffs
items.summary: Reports indicate Microsoft’s cuts have affected multiple studios, including id Software and Obsidian, while Bethesda is said to be refocusing around its biggest franchises.

items.title: Nintendo of Europe will stop selling Switch consoles in 2027
items.summary: VGC reports that Nintendo will end Switch sales through its European store in February 2027, as the company shifts focus toward newer hardware.

items.title: WayForward reveals the next Shantae game
items.summary: WayForward announced a new Shantae title at Anime Expo, with the game currently targeting a 2027 release window.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India removed import duties on some parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, eliminating 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could lower costs for manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: SWIFT launches blockchain-based shared ledger with major banks
items.summary: The global financial messaging network launched a blockchain-based shared ledger with an initial group of 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC. SWIFT says the system is intended to support round-the-clock payments and compete with stablecoin-driven alternatives.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion in Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple said it plans to spend more than $30 billion under a new chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. The deal also includes Broadcom expanding a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans in-house manufacturing for its own AI chip
items.summary: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September, according to an internal memo reported by Reuters. The company is also aiming to boost its overall computing power significantly next year.

items.title: Meta launches in-house smart glasses designed to be cheaper
items.summary: Meta announced a new line of smart glasses designed in-house, signaling a deeper push into wearables. The company is positioning the product as part of its broader technology and device strategy.

items.title: Apple raises prices on Macs and iPads amid chip shortage
items.summary: Apple increased prices on some MacBook and iPad models, citing higher memory and storage chip costs. The price pressure is being linked to the ongoing chip supply squeeze.

items.title: Intel shares rise after stronger-than-expected revenue forecast
items.summary: Intel reported a revenue outlook that beat Street estimates, lifting its shares in premarket trading. The company said it plans to increase capital spending to capitalize on the chip demand environment.

items.title: South Korean chipmakers plan massive semiconductor hub
items.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plan to invest a combined $518 billion in a new chipmaking hub. The project is aimed at meeting soaring demand for semiconductors tied to the broader tech cycle.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules on online child sexual abuse detection
items.summary: European Union lawmakers backed a proposal to reinstate temporary rules letting platforms like Google and Meta detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The move would restore enforcement powers that affect major tech platforms.

items.title: EU introduces new measures affecting steel imports and small e-commerce parcels
items.summary: The European Union unveiled two measures to protect its steel industry and limit small e-commerce parcels. The steps could affect technology-linked cross-border retail and logistics flows.
